method: Bounded public-web search of official emergency, municipal, transport, energy, air-defence, and regional-administration surfaces, followed by repository-wide canonical URL and lineage screening against the earlier strike shard plus Ukrainian-official and international-media recovery outputs. No authentication, access-control bypass, inferred date or identifier, live-warning retention, route or target detail, map capture, binary download, or full-text capture was used.

sources_checked.result: The material in-window aftermath updates resolved by the bounded pass were already represented in the Ukrainian-official recovery shard as Telegram messages 70829, 70833, and 70838. They were not duplicated as strike-infrastructure identities.

sources_checked.target: Ukrzaliznytsia public Telegram and official web surfaces
sources_checked.result: Exact-date searches did not resolve a stable publication that could be verified as 5 August 2026. Search results exposed infrastructure-attack posts without date-bearing metadata and historical material from 2025 or other 2026 dates; none was admitted by context inference.

A search result for message 14152 described rail-infrastructure damage and restoration but belongs to the 4 July 2025 Kyiv attack. It was excluded after exact-phrase and surrounding-context verification.
Exact-date searches did not resolve a stable, distinct 5 August 2026 strike or infrastructure publication with verifiable canonical identity and publication time.
Search indexing exposed port and vessel strike reports, but the visible results did not establish the assigned date and included named infrastructure and impact detail. No item was admitted.

Live warning, route, direction, and active-target material was excluded. No distinct safe retrospective publication with stable in-window metadata was resolved beyond official identities already represented elsewhere.

artifact_capture.reason: No new qualifying canonical source item was resolved, and no page bytes, map, photograph, video, or other immutable permitted artifact was downloaded, hashed, or stored.

coverage_gaps: The result is a bounded zero-item discovery outcome, not evidence that no strikes or infrastructure damage occurred during the interval.
Material DSNS aftermath and international-media publications are represented in other repository shards and were excluded here by global canonical identity rather than re-counted.
Transport, energy, municipal, and regional search indexes may lag live publisher systems or expose snippets without stable date-bearing metadata.
A prominent rail-infrastructure candidate was a 4 July 2025 historical collision, demonstrating that matching text and clock time alone are insufficient for date assignment.
Live air-defence routes, directions, targets, vulnerable facilities, named infrastructure, and granular impact detail were intentionally excluded.
No full text, images, video, maps, page bytes, or immutable artifacts were captured.
No strike, casualty, damage, interception, responsibility, or attribution assertion was independently assessed or converted into a claim, observation, territorial conclusion, or report narrative.
safety_notes: No precise current position, movement route, active-unit location, target coordinate, vulnerable-facility detail, strike geometry, or map geometry was persisted.
No authenticated platform data, private material, robots or access-control bypass, or inferred publication identity was used.
A zero-result receipt was preferred over historical-date confusion, cross-shard duplicate identities, or unsafe operational detail.
